reviews.rationale: Sequential GAAP comparison of selected SEC exhibit rows shows higher net interest income and higher noninterest income, partly offset by a larger credit loss provision and higher noninterest expense, leaving pretax and common-attributable earnings higher on a GAAP basis. The credit picture is genuinely mixed rather than uniformly improving: the annualized net chargeoff ratio is unchanged and net chargeoffs rose slightly, nonaccrual loans rose while repossessed assets fell, and the combined nonperforming-asset ratio eased only marginally; at the same time special mention loans, classified loans on accrual and classified assets all declined, and the allowance for credit losses rose. The larger provision is therefore not explained by this extract, and the allowance build alongside lower classified balances is an unresolved tension. Noninterest income strength cannot be attributed to a specific component because the loan origination and sale gain line is labeled with different scope in the two periods and is not assumed comparable. Tax expense was essentially unchanged, so it is not a driver of the earnings change. All figures are selected displayed rows, not complete filings, and no causal attribution is established. Research state is maintained at the existing conviction with no change to status; the thesis remains active and actionable.
